source.variation: The recognizer stores native writers' tablet pen traces, each resampled to 60 points. 308 of the 312 stored prototypes of the aa sign (99%) are one pen-down stroke, and 302 of the 308 start in the left third of the sign, so the bar comes first, drawn to the right. The loop's turn is the least settled part: 190 of the 308 (62%) go round it clockwise, down its right side and back up its left, and 117 go round it the other way. The bundled font prints the loop's tip tucked under the bar on the left, where the clockwise form ends, so the path follows the majority. Each sign was written by itself, with no consonant beside it, so the traces fix the sign's own strokes but not when it is written against its consonant; the book draws the sign alone and composes no Telugu word from it. The traces are scaled to a square, so they fix the start, the direction and the pen lifts, not the proportions: the path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Telugu outline of the sign on its own. The underlying HP Labs data is licensed for research use only, so only counts and shares are cited here, and no trace was copied. Handwriting varies by writer.
